label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Thank you for asking, Deirdre, and for recognising what Noma and I have built. I’m really sad about the change, though I understand it’s about the numbers and that Bronwyn needs the extra help. Noma has been with me in the Seahorses for three years, since my first year teaching, and she’s been so much more than an assistant. She helped me find my feet, from the sign-in sheets to the parent WhatsApp group, and she’s a huge part of the children’s routine and sense of security.

The first weeks of Grade R can be tough, especially with new children settling in and Charlene also being new to the class. Noma’s isiXhosa songs are part of our morning ring; the children ask for “Noma’s song” every day. And when Zayd was having meltdowns in Term 2, she was the person who could sit with him under the jungle gym and help him settle. Luthando and Mia already know her from aftercare, too. I know she’ll still be just across the courtyard, but the change will matter to the children and to me.

Could Charlene come in for a day or two during the last week of term, between 1 and 4 December, to meet Noma and see how our routine works? And could Noma pop in for morning ring during the first week back from 14 January, even for 15 minutes, if that’s possible? I think those two small steps would help make the transition easier for everyone.

Thanks again for asking rather than just announcing the change. I’m not trying to challenge the allocation, but I wanted to be honest that I’ll miss having Noma in the room and to ask for a thoughtful handover.
